high.title: Bank of Korea Holds Rates at 2.50% in New Governor's First Meeting
high.summary: The Bank of Korea maintained its benchmark interest rate at 2.50% in a widely anticipated decision, marking new Governor Shin Hyun-song's first monetary policy meeting. This decision signals continued caution as the central bank navigates inflation pressures and economic uncertainties. The rate hold reflects the BOK's balanced approach between supporting economic growth and managing price stability concerns. For FX traders, this maintains the current interest rate differential dynamics with other major currencies. Bond investors should monitor future policy signals from the new governor, as any shifts in monetary stance could significantly impact KRW government bond yields and the won's trajectory against the dollar.

high.title: Dollar-Won Surges to 1,512.90 on Middle East Tensions and Risk Aversion
high.summary: The USD/KRW exchange rate jumped 5.00 won to close at 1,512.90 in overnight trading as risk aversion intensified following Iran's threats to blockade the Strait of Hormuz and expand the Middle East front. Iran also suspended peace dialogue with the US until Israeli operations in Lebanon and Gaza cease. This represents an 8.60 won surge from the daytime session close of 1,504.30 won, highlighting how quickly geopolitical tensions can drive won weakness. The move above 1,510 suggests continued pressure on the Korean currency as safe-haven demand for dollars increases. Traders should monitor Middle East developments closely, as any escalation could push USD/KRW toward 1,520-1,530 levels, while peace progress could trigger rapid won recovery.

high.title: Seoul FX Market Focuses on US-Iran War End Timeline and Foreign Equity Outflows
high.summary: The Seoul foreign exchange market this week remains highly sensitive to potential US-Iran ceasefire developments, with a memorandum of understanding reportedly close to completion. While agreement prospects could boost risk appetite and weaken the dollar through falling oil prices, continued uncertainty and concentrated foreign stock selling are capping won gains. The dollar-won rate closed at 1,507.90 won last week after fluctuating based on negotiation sentiment and month-end flows. Key downside factors include export company settlements and war-ending expectations, while persistent foreign equity outflows limit won strength. The market's reaction to any ceasefire announcement will be crucial for determining whether the won can break below 1,500 or face further pressure toward 1,520+ levels.

medium.title: BOK Analyzes Shift from Efficiency to Security-Focused Investment Paradigm
medium.summary: The Bank of Korea released analysis showing that economic security considerations now significantly influence capital investment decisions, particularly in semiconductors. Security and global factors' contribution to investment growth expanded from 29.6% (2001-2019) to 43.9% since 2020, with trade uncertainty and geopolitical risks driving the shift. This structural change in investment patterns could affect Korea's economic growth trajectory and competitiveness.

medium.title: Korean Bond Market to Digest Government Stability Pledge and May Inflation Data
medium.summary: Korea's bond market this week will focus on US-Iran ceasefire negotiations and the government's market stabilization commitment through June treasury issuance plans. Key domestic data includes May consumer price inflation (June 2nd), while US employment data (June 5th) and ISM indices will influence global rate movements. Any ceasefire agreement could impact bonds through international oil price changes and global yield shifts.

medium.title: Atlanta Fed Slashes Q2 US Growth Forecast to 3.0%, Lowest Since Tracking Began
medium.summary: The Atlanta Fed's GDPNow model cut Q2 US growth estimates to 3.0% from 3.8%, marking the lowest forecast since tracking began. The revision reflects weaker personal consumption (2.4% vs 2.6%) and reduced private investment growth (9.3% vs 10.4%). This downward revision could influence Federal Reserve policy expectations and dollar strength, with implications for USD/KRW dynamics.

medium.title: South Korea Eyes $1 Trillion Export Milestone as May Shipments Hit Fresh Record
medium.summary: South Korea is positioned to surpass Japan as the world's fifth-largest exporter, driven by surging semiconductor demand that powered record first-quarter export performance. Strong export growth supports current account dynamics and provides fundamental support for the Korean won, though the impact may be offset by ongoing geopolitical tensions and foreign investment outflows.
